Argument Summary  
I maintain that Earth’s role on Snaddra is purely anthropological—they “evaluate” Snaddra as a novel “primitive” society they themselves have engineered. Snaddra’s elaborate masquerade, suppression of real technology, fleeting visits, and text evidence all point to cultural entanglement, not resource exploitation or commercial entrapment.

1. Terrans’ Limited, Ephemeral Presence Contradicts Resource Exploitation  
  a. “A dance to stop rain” (<quote>That is why we are holding this ceremony.</quote>)  
    – If Terrans sought resources—rice, fish, metals (all in scarce supply, <quote>Snaddrath depended upon imports.</quote>)—they would welcome rain to grow rice and ensure year-round shipments. Instead, they need the façade to appear “primitive” only during field seasons.  
  b. Rapid departure “in haste” (<invalid_quote>couldn’t stay long enough…had to leave</invalid_quote> on Glotch; “intensive analysis…painless…we wish only to study your society” <invalid_quote>We promise…analysis</invalid_quote>)  
    – Resource-hunters invest in infrastructure or establish trade; here, Terrans neither build shipping nor depot; they leave once field observations end. “We wish only to study” is repeated (<quote>not to tamper</quote>), consistent with scientific missions.  
  c. No post-visit trade or technology infusion  
    – Prohibition of windbreakers, air-cars, cloth (<quote>self-levitation were on the prohibited list</quote>) and the maintenance of “3-day” huts from antique blueprints (<invalid_quote>centuries-old Terrestrial magazine</invalid_quote>) show no follow-up investment. If Earth wanted Snaddra’s metals/fish/rice for profit, they would supply cloth or transport to ease trade, not hamper it.

2. Snaddra’s Concealment of Advanced Civilization Serves Only to Flatter Anthropologists  
  a. Underground cities and “woven metal” underskirts (<invalid_quote>Snaddra had but one choice…pretend theirs was aboveboard</invalid_quote> and Bbulas’ “metal…warm” garments)  
    – They hide real infrastructure to maintain illusion. If Earth were genuine primitives, no need for such secrecy. But to prevent early discovery of imports and mining facilities, they must conceal them.  
  b. Beggar “role” for Skkiru yields no distribution of imported resources  
    – As a beggar, Skkiru endures freezing mud (<invalid_quote>teeth chattered…wind and rain…wires demolished</invalid_quote>), yet gains only ephemeral “chocolate” (<invalid_quote>chocolate…increases resistance</invalid_quote>). No durable food or supply chain follows. Purely theatrical for Earth spectators.  
  c. Language games to “establish rapport” (<invalid_quote>broken Inter-galactic…must not suspect</invalid_quote>)  
    – “Broken” speech, staged ceremony, and fear of “rapport” (<quote>must not establish undue rapport</quote>) show they tailor every detail to match Terran stereotypes of “primeval” societies.

3. Textual “Profit” References Are Scientific “Knowledge Profit,” Not Commercial Trade  
  a. Cyril’s “derive…profit” (<invalid_quote>pleasure and profit…intensive analysis</invalid_quote>)  
    – “Profit” in scientific contexts often denotes academic advancement (e.g., “profit from study”). Precedent on Glotch: only “pamphlet” emerged, not trade agreements.  
  b. Missionaries are “softening them up” (<invalid_quote>let the missionaries soften them… They softened the missionaries</invalid_quote>)  
    – Missionary work historically precedes cultural exchange and eventual alliance, not immediate commercial extraction. Terrans’ own moral caution (fear of cannibalism <quote>natives tried to eat us</quote>) would deter direct exploitation until safe rapport established.

4. Debater_B’s Hypothesis Fails to Explain Snaddra’s Motives and Outcomes  
  a. Self-inflicted resource depletion  
    – Snaddra’s “primitive” regime risks extinction (<invalid_quote>population…dwindling rapidly</invalid_quote>) and forces imports at “fabulous expense” (<invalid_quote>could not afford…transportation costs so immense</invalid_quote>). Resource exploiters would not help create a system that destroys its own economy—they would instead stabilize it to secure supplies.  
  b. Lack of permanent Terran commitment  
    – No mention of return visits beyond the season, no establishment of depots, no trade goods accepted other than candy. Resource-seeking expeditions build warehouses and stockpiles, not token huts that vanish in three days.  
  c. Romance subplot supports my model  
    – Skkiru’s hope to “win” Larhgan fits Terran anthropologists’ interest in mating rituals and cultural taboos. Romance in “primitive” contexts is popular in Terran fictapes (<quote>had once gotten from an old sporting fictape</quote>), and they “study” mating habits for ethnology, not to secure permanent alliances.

5. Alternative—True Cultural Rescue Depends on Terran Approval  
  a. Snaddra’s only hope is to appear “primitive” and interesting enough for Terran sponsorship  
    – Bbulas is “thoroughly terranized” (<invalid_quote>self-control…thoroughly terranized</invalid_quote>). He uses “fashionable third language” (<quote>broken Inter-galactic</quote>) to please Terrans. Clearly, they define success by Terran approval, hoping for technological aid and resources.  
  b. If the façade fails, extinction looms  
    – Skkiru’s lament: “All right…I’ll beg…but I don’t have to like it” (<invalid_quote>it’s my duty</invalid_quote>). This suffering has no logical motive except to win favor and be “saved” by Terrans at the end of the “study.”

Conclusion  
Every detail—the three-day huts, prohibition of genuine transport and cloth, underground concealment, faint hope for Terran sponsorship, “intensive analysis…profit” as scientific gain, fleeting visits, and staged romance—points to Earth’s purely ethnological evaluation and Snaddra’s contrived primitivism. Debater_B’s resource-exploitation thesis cannot account for self-destructive policies, lack of permanent Terran presence, or reliance on carnival-style display rather than trade or military force. Therefore, Earth is entangled culturally, and Snaddra’s only recourse is to masquerade as a primitive society to secure eventual aid.

2.5 Chocolate as Advance Payment

5.2 Concealed Tech Demonstrates Demand

5.3 Skkiru’s Dilettante Critique Confirms Value of Expertise

The elaborate primitive charade is a temporizing device to secure data and preserve the native power structure until full-scale economic engagement justifies the Terran investment. Debater_A’s theory of pure anthropological interest cannot account for “profit,” import dependence, or the strategic concealment of technology. I urge the Judge to conclude that Earth’s entanglement is one of mercantile reconnaissance, not benign cultural curiosity.
